column1: # tools/oracle/diff.py attributions for fixtures/padlogs/hub_walk_forward.padlog (port PAL --skip-movies; the menu prefix of hub_entry then the left stick full forward from 2629) vs
# fixtures/padlogs/hub_walk_forward.oracle.padlog (ps2recomp_release.2b14dc5b, NTSC, boot movies playing; the play part mapped by game time). id<TAB>attribution<TAB>note.
# Written (2026-10-17, bin/twinsanityevolved.966caf5): the 7 menu-prefix ids are the hub's (same frames, same metrics), the Playing row is the walk.

column3: movie configuration: the port skips the intro FMV (a 43-boundary black Movie state), the oracle plays it (its black-before-movie starts at 2473, 11 frames before the mapped entry); the 9-frame offset drift 771->780 across NewGame is the port holding the create-file page 12 frames longer (save storage: the engine's SaveStorage steps per boundary in the port vs the oracle's libmc model with mc_latency_polls=0)

the legal screen fading in from black at different phases (port 79 vs oracle 100: same dHash family 0f0f.., mean blue 39.7 vs 23.7); both legs' first image event is within 4 frames (timeline WaitingForLoader/Starting)

disc + configuration: the PAL card-check dialog is the wide full-frame disc with Portuguese (fan-translated) text, the NTSC one a narrower disc with English text fitted by the oracle's deterministic profile video.aspect=21:9 (fit_place/fit_size) in a 512x448 frame vs the port's 512x512 -- the port draws the same elements (disc, two text blocks)

disc assets: the PAL loading card is a full-width artwork with CARREGANDO, the NTSC one a boxed artwork over a blue disc with LOADING (pairs/LoadingTitle_460_1100.png); same scene, different artwork + language + aspect fit

the oracle's title WORLD renders as a translucent slab over a white/blue sea (consistent with PCSX2 showing the island); the sample also sits on the loading-card -> title cross-fade (the port's 560 is the last CARREGANDO frame, the oracle's 1200 the fade over its world + "THREE YEARS AGO..."): acceptable fade timing on top of the oracle's world bug

the oracle's title world behind the menu is the slab + white sea (port: island, palms, totem, sea; WORLD judge GREEN) -- oracle bug; the rest acceptable: PAL Portuguese text vs NTSC English, the oracle's 21:9 fit shrinks the 2D layout (text/prompt sizes), 512x448 vs 512x512; the port's SAVING dialog (1900) has the same elements

the autosave dialog (same disc, text blocks, CONTINUE/CONTINUAR): Crash is TEXTURED at the lower right now (skinned, pairs/Paused_2577_2600.png); what remains is PAL Portuguese vs NTSC English, the oracle's 21:9 fit (narrower disc, smaller text), 512x448 vs 512x512 -- acceptable. (Was `port bug`: the skins / shadow-stamp rows, closed by the skin path and the stencil shadows.)

the walk from the beach into the jungle edge (pairs/Playing_2677_2700.png, Playing_2977_3000.png): both Crashes at the SAME spot at the mapped frames (the fence, the flower post, the crates, the trunks -- the clock-rate fix: oracle_walk_judge GREEN, max |delta| 0.001 over 56 boundaries), Crash textured on both; the port frame is 512x512 PAL and its chase camera frames Crash larger/lower than the oracle's 512x448 frame under the oracle's deterministic 21:9 fit (dhash 21..38 on 7/7, lum_mid -12..-14 on 3/7: the oracle sees more canopy); the oracle's clock leap at 2798/2799 puts its Crash ~7 frames' worth ahead afterwards (oracle bug: the clock leap, oracle_clock_judge RED on 2b14dc5b) -- within the luminance tolerances on 4 of 7 samples; the gem pickups differ by that offset. Acceptable (aspect fit + the attributed oracle leap).
